'''Roman Bezrukavnikov''' ([[Russian language|Russian]]: Роман Безрукавников; born July 1, 1973) is a Russian-American [[mathematician]] born in [[Moscow]].<ref name=cv>{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae|work=Roman Bezrukavnikov's Home Page|publisher=[[MIT]]|url=http://math.mit.edu/~bezrukav/cv.pdf|access-date=8 March 2020}}</ref> He is a mathematics professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and the chief research fellow at the [[HSE Faculty of Mathematics|HSE International Laboratory of Representation Theory and Mathematical Physics]] who specializes in [[representation theory]] and [[algebraic geometry]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thecrimson.com/article.aspx?ref=517052|title=Harvard Destroys MIT In Cantab Dance-Off |last=Flow|first=Christian B. |date= February 15, 2007|work=Harvard Crimson|access-date=2009-10-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mf.hse.ru/en/persons|title = International Laboratory of Representation Theory and Mathematical Physics}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
He graduated from [[Moscow State School 57]] mathematical class in 1990,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sch57.ru/people/alumni/#y1990|title= Alumni list|publisher=Moscow School 57}}</ref> and earned an [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] at [[Brandeis University]] in 1994.{{r|cv}}  He received his [[doctor of philosophy|Ph.D.]] in mathematics from [[Tel Aviv University]] in 1998 under the supervision of [[Joseph N. Bernstein]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|87772}}</ref>

Bezrukavnikov was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 1996-1998 and again in 2007–2008.<ref>[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/ Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars]</ref> He was a Dickson Instructor at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1999-2001. In 2001 he was awarded a [[Clay Research Fellowship]],<ref name=clay>{{cite web|title=Roman Bezrukavnikov|work=Research Fellows|publisher=[[Clay Mathematics Institute]]|url=https://www.claymath.org/people/roman-bezrukavnikov|access-date=8 March 2020}}</ref> and in 2004, he won a [[Sloan Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellowship]] from the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dailynorthwestern.com/2.13924/math-professor-granted-distinguished-fellowship-1.1971448 |title=Math professor granted distinguished fellowship |last=Meron |first=Deborah |date=April 6, 2004 |work=The Daily Northwestern |access-date=2009-10-26 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091029164906/http://www.dailynorthwestern.com/2.13924/math-professor-granted-distinguished-fellowship-1.1971448 |archive-date=October 29, 2009 }}</ref><ref name=sloan>{{cite web|title=Past fellows|publisher=[[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]]|url=https://sloan.org/past-fellows?page=184|access-date=8 March 2020}}</ref>  He was awarded a Simons Fellowship in Mathematics by the [[Simons Foundation]] in 2014, and again in 2020.<ref name=simons>{{cite web|title=Simons Fellows in Mathematics|date=19 June 2012|publisher=[[Simons Foundation]]|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-fellows-in-mathematics/?tab=awardees|access-date=8 March 2020}}</ref>
